title: Campaign & Collaboration Policy

intro.text: This Policy governs the responsibilities of both parties once a brief has been accepted and a Collaboration has commenced. It is intended to make expectations explicit and to provide a predictable process where things go wrong.

head: Stage
What happens
rows: Brand sends a brief to a Creator specifying deliverables, timeline and fee.
Either party may propose changes. Nothing is binding until acceptance.
Both parties agree scope, fee and timeline. Terms are recorded on the Platform.
Brand funds the agreed amount in full. Work should not begin before this.
Creator produces the content within the agreed timeline.
Creator submits deliverables through the Platform.
Brand approves, or requests revisions within scope, within 7 days.
Content is published as agreed and payment is released to the Creator.

blocks.text: The agreed scope is that recorded on the Platform at the point of acceptance. Any change to deliverables, timeline, usage rights or exclusivity must be agreed in writing through the Platform and, where it increases the work required, may attract an additional fee.

items: A Creator should deliver by the agreed date and must notify the Brand promptly if delay is unavoidable.
A Brand must review submitted work within 7 days and either approve it or request revisions within scope.

Automatic completion — if a Brand neither approves nor requests revisions within 7 days of submission, the Collaboration is treated as completed and payment is released to the Creator. This protects Creators from indefinite delay.

blocks.text: Unless otherwise agreed, a Creator will provide up to two rounds of revision where the request is within the originally agreed scope. A request that materially changes the concept, format, messaging, platform or deliverable count is a new scope, not a revision, and may be charged separately.

A request for revision must be specific and must identify what in the submitted work does not meet the agreed brief. A rejection expressed only as dissatisfaction, without identifying a departure from the brief, is not a valid revision request. Where a Brand does not provide specific written reasons within 7 days of submission, the Collaboration is treated as approved under clause 5.3.

sections.heading: Where content is still not approved after the agreed revisions

blocks.text: This clause applies where the Creator has delivered the original work and completed the agreed rounds of revision, and the Brand still declines to approve. The Collaboration moves to Resolution. Neither party is required to continue working, and the Creator is not required to produce further revisions without additional payment.

The governing principle is that a Brand may not obtain unlimited work by repeatedly withholding approval, and a Creator may not be paid in full for work that does not meet the agreed brief. The parties may settle the matter themselves under options A to C, failing which either may escalate under option D.

head: Option
What happens
Money
rows: A. Accept at a reduced fee
The Brand accepts and uses the work as delivered, at a fee reduced by agreement.
Agreed reduced amount released to the Creator; balance refunded.
The Brand requests additional changes and the Creator agrees to make them. Charged as new scope.
Original amount held; additional fee funded before further work begins.
Neither party wishes to continue. The Collaboration ends. The Brand receives no licence and must not use the work in any form.
50% of the agreed fee released to the Creator for work performed; 50% refunded to the Brand.
Either party refers the matter to Marqueiver under Policy 10.

blocks.text: If the parties do not agree on A, B or C within 7 days of the final revision being rejected, option C applies automatically, unless either party has escalated under option D.

sections.heading: How a dispute over rejected content is determined

This Policy governs the responsibilities of both parties once a brief has been accepted and a Collaboration has commenced. It is intended to make expectations explicit and to provide a predictable process where things go wrong.

## 5.1 Lifecycle of a Collaboration

Stage | What happens
--- | ---
Invitation | Brand sends a brief to a Creator specifying deliverables, timeline and fee.
Negotiation | Either party may propose changes. Nothing is binding until acceptance.
Acceptance | Both parties agree scope, fee and timeline. Terms are recorded on the Platform.
Escrow funding | Brand funds the agreed amount in full. Work should not begin before this.
In progress | Creator produces the content within the agreed timeline.
Submission | Creator submits deliverables through the Platform.
Review | Brand approves, or requests revisions within scope, within 7 days.
Completion | Content is published as agreed and payment is released to the Creator.

## 5.2 Scope

The agreed scope is that recorded on the Platform at the point of acceptance. Any change to deliverables, timeline, usage rights or exclusivity must be agreed in writing through the Platform and, where it increases the work required, may attract an additional fee.

## 5.3 Timelines and review

- A Creator should deliver by the agreed date and must notify the Brand promptly if delay is unavoidable.
- A Brand must review submitted work within 7 days and either approve it or request revisions within scope.
- Automatic completion — if a Brand neither approves nor requests revisions within 7 days of submission, the Collaboration is treated as completed and payment is released to the Creator. This protects Creators from indefinite delay.

## 5.4 Revisions

Unless otherwise agreed, a Creator will provide up to two rounds of revision where the request is within the originally agreed scope. A request that materially changes the concept, format, messaging, platform or deliverable count is a new scope, not a revision, and may be charged separately.

A request for revision must be specific and must identify what in the submitted work does not meet the agreed brief. A rejection expressed only as dissatisfaction, without identifying a departure from the brief, is not a valid revision request. Where a Brand does not provide specific written reasons within 7 days of submission, the Collaboration is treated as approved under clause 5.3.

## 5.5 Where content is still not approved after the agreed revisions

This clause applies where the Creator has delivered the original work and completed the agreed rounds of revision, and the Brand still declines to approve. The Collaboration moves to Resolution. Neither party is required to continue working, and the Creator is not required to produce further revisions without additional payment.

The governing principle is that a Brand may not obtain unlimited work by repeatedly withholding approval, and a Creator may not be paid in full for work that does not meet the agreed brief. The parties may settle the matter themselves under options A to C, failing which either may escalate under option D.

Option | What happens | Money
--- | --- | ---
A. Accept at a reduced fee | The Brand accepts and uses the work as delivered, at a fee reduced by agreement. | Agreed reduced amount released to the Creator; balance refunded.
B. Further paid revision | The Brand requests additional changes and the Creator agrees to make them. Charged as new scope. | Original amount held; additional fee funded before further work begins.
C. Release without use (default settlement) | Neither party wishes to continue. The Collaboration ends. The Brand receives no licence and must not use the work in any form. | 50% of the agreed fee released to the Creator for work performed; 50% refunded to the Brand.
D. Escalate to dispute | Either party refers the matter to Marqueiver under Policy 10. | Funds held until determination.

If the parties do not agree on A, B or C within 7 days of the final revision being rejected, option C applies automatically, unless either party has escalated under option D.

## 5.6 How a dispute over rejected content is determined

Where the matter is escalated, Marqueiver assesses the submitted work against the brief recorded at the point of acceptance, together with the in-platform record of the revision requests. Our determination follows these principles:

Finding | Outcome
--- | ---
The work materially meets the agreed brief; the objection is one of taste or preference | Full payment released to the Creator. The Brand may use the work.
The work meets the brief in part; some agreed elements are missing or incomplete | Partial release, usually between 50% and 75%, reflecting the work properly performed.
The work materially fails the agreed brief — for example wrong product, wrong format, wrong platform, or unusable quality | Full refund to the Brand, or one final opportunity to correct where the Creator requests it.
The brief was unclear, or the Brand changed its requirements after acceptance | Full or substantially full payment to the Creator. Ambiguity and changes of mind are the Brand's risk, not the Creator's.

## 5.7 Protections against misuse

- A Brand that declines to approve work has no licence to use it. Publishing, adapting or otherwise using rejected content makes the full agreed fee immediately payable, in addition to any remedy for breach of Policy 8.
- Repeatedly rejecting work after full revision cycles, across multiple Collaborations, is treated as an attempt to obtain unpaid work and may result in restriction or suspension under Policy 12.
- A Creator who submits work plainly unrelated to the brief, or who submits the same work unchanged in response to a valid revision request, is not entitled to the settlement in option C.
- Where a Brand supplied a product for review or use, and the Collaboration ends under this clause, the Brand may request its return at its own cost unless the item was consumed in good faith performance of the brief.

## 5.8 Publication and content longevity

Where publication is a deliverable, the Creator must publish on the agreed platform, at the agreed time, with the disclosures required by Policy 15. Unless otherwise agreed, published content must remain live for a minimum of 30 days. Early removal without cause may result in partial or full refund to the Brand.

## 5.9 Performance

Neither Marqueiver nor the Creator guarantees any level of reach, engagement, conversion or sales. Payment is for the agreed deliverables, not for a commercial outcome, unless the parties have expressly agreed a performance-based arrangement.

## 5.10 Confidentiality

Campaign details, unreleased products and any information marked confidential must not be disclosed before the agreed publication date, and thereafter only to the extent published.

## 5.11 Failure to perform

- If a Creator fails to deliver by the agreed date and does not agree a revised date, the Brand may cancel and receive a refund under Policy 7.
- If a Brand fails to provide materials or information necessary for the work, timelines extend accordingly.
- Persistent failure by either party may lead to action under Policy 12.

This Policy explains how money moves through the Platform: Credits purchased by Brands, funding and release of Collaboration payments, refunds, and the treatment of taxes.

- Credits are not transferable between accounts, carry no interest, and may not be exchanged for cash except as set out above.

## 6.2 Collaboration payments and escrow

Collaboration amounts are funded by the Brand before work commences and are held by our payment partner until release. Funds are released to the Creator upon Brand approval, upon automatic completion under Policy 5.3, or upon determination of a dispute under Policy 10.

## 6.3 Platform commission

Marqueiver charges a platform commission of 12.5% of the Collaboration value. Commission is deducted at the point of release, so the Creator receives the agreed amount less the commission and any statutory deductions. Commission is set out in full in Policy 14.

## 6.4 Payouts to Creators

- Payouts are made to the UPI ID or bank account registered in the Creator's own name.
- Payouts are initiated within 3 working days of release and typically settle within a further 2 working days, subject to banking timelines.
- Marqueiver is not liable for delay or loss caused by incorrect payout details supplied by the Creator.

## 6.5 Refunds to Brands

Situation | Outcome
--- | ---
Creator declines or does not respond | Full refund of the escrowed amount.
Cancelled before work begins | Full refund of the escrowed amount.
Cancelled after work has begun | Pro-rata settlement — see Policy 7.
Creator fails to deliver | Full refund, subject to review.
Deliverables materially not as agreed | Full or partial refund on determination under Policy 10.
Brand changes its mind after delivery | No refund. Work has been performed.

Marqueiver is not presently registered under GST. No GST is charged on Credits, on Collaboration amounts, or on the platform commission. The amounts displayed on the Platform are the amounts payable in full.

Marqueiver will register under GST when required to do so, and expects to do so as paid transactions commence on the Platform. The following applies from the date of registration:

- From the date of registration, a tax invoice will be issued in place of a payment receipt, and Brands should provide their GSTIN to claim input credit where eligible.

Where a payment fails, we will notify you and may retry. Where a chargeback or payment dispute is raised, we may suspend related Collaborations and Credits pending resolution.

All transactions are in Indian Rupees (INR).

This Policy explains what Marqueiver charges, when it is charged, and what it pays for. Our aim is that there are no surprises on either side.

## 14.1 Platform commission — 12.5%

Marqueiver charges a platform commission of 12.5% of the agreed Collaboration value. The commission is deducted at the point funds are released to the Creator. The Creator therefore receives the agreed amount less the 12.5% commission and any statutory deductions such as tax deducted at source.

--- | ---

Marqueiver commission at 12.5% | ₹1,250
Statutory deductions (illustrative, if applicable) | As required by law
Net amount payable to the Creator | ₹8,750 less any statutory deduction

Figures are illustrative. No GST is added at present, as Marqueiver is not yet registered. Any TDS applies only where required by law — see Policy 6.8, under which most Creators will see no deduction.

## 14.3 What the commission covers

- Discovery, matching and profile analysis.
- Escrow handling and payment processing.
- In-platform communication and the transaction record.
- Dispute resolution and support.
- Fraud prevention and verification.

## 14.4 What Creators pay

Creators pay nothing to join, to build a profile, to be discovered or to receive briefs. The only deduction from a Creator is the commission on a completed Collaboration. Optional paid visibility tiers are separate, entirely voluntary, and are described in Policy 3.9.

## 14.5 What Brands pay

- Credits, purchased in advance, to access Creator information (Policy 6.1).
- The Collaboration value, funded into escrow before work begins.

The 12.5% commission is deducted from the Collaboration value and is not charged additionally to the Brand, unless expressly agreed otherwise.

## 14.6 Taxes on fees

Marqueiver is not presently registered under GST, and no GST is charged on the platform commission. A payment receipt is issued for each commission charged.

Amounts are quoted exclusive of taxes. Marqueiver will register under GST when required to do so, expected as paid transactions commence. From that date GST will be added at the prevailing statutory rate, tax invoices will replace payment receipts, and at least 15 days' notice will be given. Credits already purchased and Collaborations already accepted will not be taxed retrospectively. Full detail is at Policy 6.7.

Deductions from Creator payouts are made only where required under the Income-tax Act 1961. See Policy 6.8.

## 14.7 Changes to fees

We may change commission rates or Credit pricing on at least 30 days' notice given by email and in-platform notice. Changes do not affect Collaborations already accepted, or Credits already purchased.

## 14.8 Promotional rates

We may from time to time offer reduced or zero commission for particular campaigns, cohorts or periods. Where we do, the applicable rate is that shown at the point of acceptance of the Collaboration.

Every paid partnership arranged through Marqueiver must be disclosed clearly. This is a legal requirement in India under the ASCI Guidelines for Influencer Advertising in Digital Media and the Consumer Protection Act 2019, and it is a condition of using the Platform.

## 15.1 When disclosure is required

Disclosure is required wherever a Creator has received anything of value in exchange for content. This includes monetary payment, free products, gifting, discounts, travel, hospitality, affiliate commission or any other benefit — whether or not the Brand asked for a specific message.

## 15.2 How to disclose

- Use a clear label such as #ad, #advertisement, #sponsored, #paidpartnership, #collab or #brandambassador, or the platform's own paid-partnership tool.
- Place the disclosure prominently and upfront, so that it is visible without the viewer having to click More, expand a caption or scroll.
- In video, the disclosure must be visible or audible for a sufficient period to be noticed, and not only in the description.
- In audio or live content, state the disclosure verbally at the start.
- Use the same language as the content itself, so that a Hindi or regional-language audience understands it.

## 15.3 Labels that are not acceptable

- Vague or ambiguous terms such as #collab used alone without context, #sp, #thanks or #gifted where it is unclear a commercial arrangement exists.
- Disclosure buried among a large block of unrelated hashtags.
- Disclosure visible only after expanding the caption.
- Disclosure in a language the audience is unlikely to understand.

## 15.4 Substantiation of claims

- Do not state or imply results that cannot be substantiated by the Brand.
- Health, medical, nutritional, financial and income claims require particular care and must be supported by the Brand with evidence.
- Do not present a personal opinion as clinical or expert advice unless suitably qualified.
- Do not disparage a competitor without a factual basis.

## 15.5 Responsibilities

Creators — are responsible for making the disclosure correctly on every piece of paid content, and for verifying claims they make about a product.

Brands — must not ask a Creator to omit or obscure a disclosure, and must provide substantiation for any claim they require a Creator to make. A Brand that instructs a Creator to conceal a commercial relationship is in breach of this Policy.

Marqueiver — provides guidance and may check published content for compliance, but is not responsible for a Creator's or Brand's failure to comply with law.

## 15.6 Special categories

Content relating to alcohol, tobacco, betting and gambling, real-money gaming, financial products, cryptocurrency, medicines, medical devices, infant nutrition and children's products is subject to additional legal restrictions, and in some cases outright prohibition. Refer to Policy 11.3 and take independent advice before proceeding.

## 15.7 Consequences of non-disclosure

- We may require the content to be corrected or removed.
- Payment may be withheld until the disclosure is corrected.
- Repeated failure may result in suspension or termination.
- Regulatory penalties under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 fall on the Creator and the Brand, not on Marqueiver.
